title: Feature request: canonical reproducibility-bundle export in scripts/
body:
## What's already there

\`--output_path\` already saves \`git_hash\`, task versions, model config, and per-sample outputs via \`--log_samples\`. \`--check_integrity\` validates task definitions. \`scripts/model_comparator.py\` and \`scripts/regression.py\` show the existing pattern for post-processing tools.

## What's missing

A lightweight canonical hash of results for cross-run comparison. The hashing utilities in \`utils.py\` (SHA256, deterministic ordering) exist but aren't surfaced in the output for external verification. Per-sample logs can be very large; a compact fingerprint of the outputs would let two parties confirm they got the same answers without shipping multi-GB files.

## Proposal

A \`scripts/export_attestation.py\` post-processing tool — consuming the existing \`--output_path --log_samples\` outputs — that emits a small, self-describing JSON document:

\`\`\`json
{
  "model_id": "<provider/name>",
  "tasks": ["<task_id>", "..."],
  "results": [
    {"task_id": "...", "metric": "...", "value": 0.847, "stderr": 0.025}
  ],
  "results_sha256": "<sha256 of canonical encoding of model_id + tasks + results>",
  "outputs_sha256": "<sha256 of per-sample outputs>"
}
\`\`\`

The metadata fields are included alongside the hashes so the bundle is independently interpretable — a reader can see what was attested and recompute the hashes themselves to verify. Two hashes, doing different work:

- **\`results_sha256\`** — an independent re-run reaching identical headline scores produces the same digest, enabling cross-run comparison without exchanging full log files.
- **\`outputs_sha256\`** — catches divergent outputs that roll up to the same headline score (compensating errors, filter differences). If \`results_sha256\` matches but \`outputs_sha256\` doesn't, that's a flag worth investigating.

Intentionally minimal: stdlib only, no new dependencies, consumes files already on disk.

## Why it'd be useful

- **Audit trails.** When eval scores are cited, the bundle lets readers ask for the artefact and verify it matches.
- **Cross-org reproduction.** Two labs running the same eval can compare bundles without shipping logs.
- **Drift detection.** \`outputs_sha256\` diverging while \`results_sha256\` holds is a signal the existing tooling doesn't surface.

## Where this came up

While building [Valichord](https://github.com/topeuph-ai/ValiChord), a decentralised verification protocol for AI eval claims — we needed a canonical attestation format covering runs from multiple harnesses. An analogous tool is currently open as a PR against [UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_evals](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_evals/pull/1610). Happy to draft a PR here in the same shape if there's interest.

title: Scalar `seed` in a YAML config crashes with TypeError; `seed: 0` silently disables seeding
body:
## Summary

`seed` is documented as `list/int` in `docs/config_files.md`, but a scalar seed in a YAML `--config` file is never expanded the way `--seed` is on the command line, so `lm_eval --config cfg.yaml` crashes before evaluation starts.

```yaml
# cfg.yaml
model: hf
tasks: arc_easy
seed: 42
```

```
TypeError: 'int' object is not subscriptable
```

It comes from `lm_eval/_cli/run.py:420-423`:

```python
random_seed=cfg.seed[0] if cfg.seed else None,
numpy_random_seed=cfg.seed[1] if cfg.seed else None,
torch_random_seed=cfg.seed[2] if cfg.seed else None,
fewshot_random_seed=cfg.seed[3] if cfg.seed else None,
```

Those four accessors assume the value has already been expanded to a 4-list. On the CLI path that is true, because argparse runs it through `_int_or_none_list_arg_type` first (`run.py:313`). A value read from a config file goes into `EvaluatorConfig` untouched, and its `seed` field is declared `seed: list` with no coercion.

So the same documented value behaves differently depending on how it is supplied:

```
--seed 42          ->  [42, 42, 42, 42]     works
seed: 42 in YAML   ->  42                   TypeError
```

## Other shapes

Two more cases fall out of the same gap, and one of them is quiet:

| config value | result |
| --- | --- |
| `seed: 42` | `TypeError: 'int' object is not subscriptable` |
| `seed: 0` | no seeding at all, silently: `0` is falsy, so every `if cfg.seed` guard takes the `None` branch |
| `seed: [42]` | `IndexError: list index out of range` |
| `seed: "42"` | seeds with the character `"4"`, since `cfg.seed[0]` indexes the string |

`seed: 0` is the one worth flagging. Someone pinning a seed for reproducibility gets a run with no seeding and no warning.

`seed: [0,1234,1234,1234]` and `seed: null` both behave correctly today.

## Reproduction

No model backend needed:

```python
from lm_eval.config.evaluate_config import EvaluatorConfig

cfg = EvaluatorConfig(tasks=["arc_easy"], seed=42)._configure()
cfg.seed[0]        # TypeError: 'int' object is not subscriptable

cfg = EvaluatorConfig(tasks=["arc_easy"], seed=0)._configure()
cfg.seed[0] if cfg.seed else None      # None, i.e. not seeded
```

## Fix

Normalizing `seed` inside `EvaluatorConfig` so both entry points end up with the same shape looks like the smallest fix, and it matches how the CLI converter already behaves for every accepted input (1 value replicated, 3 values filled from defaults with a warning, 4 values kept, anything else rejected).

I have that written with tests and will open a PR referencing this issue.

title: `_parse_dict_args` is a no-op under postponed annotations, and `DICT_KEYS` is unused
body:
## Summary

`EvaluatorConfig._parse_dict_args` can never do anything, because the module uses postponed annotation evaluation:

```python
# lm_eval/config/evaluate_config.py:1
from __future__ import annotations
...
# :267
def _parse_dict_args(self):
    # Parse string arguments that should be dictionaries
    for f in fields(self):
        if f.type is dict and isinstance(getattr(self, f.name), str):
            setattr(self, f.name, simple_parse_args_string(getattr(self, f.name)))
    return self
```

With `from __future__ import annotations`, `dataclasses.fields()` reports `f.type` as the **string** `"dict"`, not the `dict` type, so `f.type is dict` is never true:

```python
from __future__ import annotations
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, fields

@dataclass
class Demo:
    model_args: dict = field(default_factory=dict)

f = fields(Demo)[0]
f.type            # 'dict'   (a str)
f.type is dict    # False
f.type == "dict"  # True
```

The method is called on the config-file path (`cls(**config)._parse_dict_args()` at :224), so it runs — it just never converts anything.

## The related loose end

`DICT_KEYS` is defined at :21 and, as far as I can tell, is never referenced anywhere in the codebase:

```python
DICT_KEYS = [
    "wandb_args", "wandb_config_args", "hf_hub_log_args",
    "metadata", "model_args", "gen_kwargs",
]
```

`grep -rn "DICT_KEYS" lm_eval` returns only that definition. It lists exactly the fields `_parse_dict_args` looks like it was meant to cover, so I suspect the two were intended to be used together and the name-based check was replaced by the type-based one at some point.

## What I'm unsure about

The documented config shape for these fields is a nested mapping, and that path works fine today:

```yaml
model_args:
  pretrained: gpt2
  dtype: float32
```

So the no-op only matters if the CLI string form is also meant to be accepted in a config file:

```yaml
model_args: "pretrained=gpt2,dtype=float32"
```

That's a natural thing to paste in from `--model_args`, and `simple_parse_args_string` exists precisely to parse it, but I don't want to assert it's a supported shape when the docs only show the mapping.

## Question

Is the string form meant to work in a config file? If yes, the fix is small — switch the check to the field name (`f.name in DICT_KEYS`, which also gives `DICT_KEYS` a use) or compare against the annotation string — and I'm happy to send it with tests. If not, then `_parse_dict_args` and `DICT_KEYS` are both dead and could probably just be removed.

title: [Proposal] OpenEval Import/Export Support
body:
## Overview

We have launched [OpenEval](https://github.com/adhabnr-ux/openeval) (v1.0.0-rc.1), an open standard (Apache 2.0) for portable LLM evaluation datasets. Every eval framework uses incompatible formats — OpenEval provides a standard JSON format + converters + SDKs (TypeScript + Python).

## What We're Proposing

Add `to_openeval()` and `from_openeval()` methods (~50-100 lines using our SDK).

## Resources

- **Spec:** https://github.com/adhabnr-ux/openeval/blob/main/spec/SPEC.md
- **npm SDK:** `npm install @openeval/sdk`
- **PyPI SDK:** `pip install openeval`

We would love to collaborate.

title: max_model_length for gemma3-12b is set to 2048 (_DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH) with the hf processor
body:
There is this line in the hf processor:  https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/blob/59b3ba263be2c6ac7f60a4b6a1219f8a8acb552b/lm_eval/models/huggingface.py#L468
```        if hasattr(self.tokenizer, "model_max_length"):
            if self.tokenizer.model_max_length == TOKENIZER_INFINITY:
                return self._DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH
```

I wonder why is this the case? I am evaluating gemma3-12b which has `model_max_length = TOKENIZER_INFINITY  =  1000000000000000019884624838656`
this sets the max_length to only 2048 (_DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH). Is this intended?
